newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol sees good business division outlook.
newsitem.headline: Repsol sees good business division outlook.

text.p: Spanish energy group Repsol SA forecast a strong outlook for its various businesses on Wednesday in a presentation of the share offer to institutional investors.
The government is in the process of selling its remaining 10.0 percent stake after which the firm will be fully privatised.
REFINING AND MARKETING
"Prospects, both in refining and in marketing are good," said division director Antonio Gonzalez-Adalid, adding that the firm would continue to benefit from cost advantages versus its competitors.

"Even under the conservative scenario we have used (for the forecasts) which assumes that refining and marketing margins stay at the same levels as in 1996, we expect to see annual average growth of over 10 percent in the next five years," he said.

Between 1997 and 2001, the firm aims to increase its reserves by 20 percent by developing fields in strategic areas and by buying new reserves. It will particularly concentrate on developing integrated gas systems in Latin America and North Africa.
The firm was optimistic on the division's outlook because of the strategic location of the refineries and the progressive recovery of transformation margins.
Marketing is seeing the benefits of a more aggressive pricing policy started in September.

"We've gone from selling petrol at practically the same price throughout Spain to a specific price policy at each sale point, taking into account it's competitive position. This allows us to recover market share" he said.
Sales are expected to increase two percent annually, while investments will be half last year's amount annually.
Repsol anticipates an improvement in efficiency, and product quality.
CHEMICALS
This division will benefit from the development of more value-added products, increased productivity and reduced costs, Gonzalez-Adalid said.

Production capacity for intermediate products such as propylene oxide will be increased. "This will allow us to grow in high-yielding markets and at the same time reduce our exposure to market volatility," he said.
Chemical derivative profits are expected to have doubled by 1999.
LIQUID PETROLEUM GAS (LPG)
This market has substantial growth potential, and Repsol expects the price capping system to be reintroduced, Gonzalez-Adalid said.
This area will see reduced costs and growth will be boosted by bulk sales. LPG prices are expected to increase short term.
Operating results for the next five years will be in line with annual growth of 13 percent in the past few years.
NATURAL GAS
Repsol expects natural gas consumption to double between 1996 and the end of the decade, evolving similarly until 2010.
"We expect results in this division to increase two and a half times from now to the year 2001", Gonzalez-Adalid said.
ELECTRICITY

"Repsol, like other oil firms, sees significant opportunities in new projects derived from the integration of our gas business and the possibility of generating electricity from refinery residues," said chairman Alfonso Cortina.
"This will allow us to develop a highly-profitable business based on existing activities."
Repsol has an agreement to develop electricity business with Gas Natural and Iberdrola.
